verification_report.summary: The proof is correct under the stated accepted inputs. The strongly Gauduchon form controls the h-mass through a fixed de Rham pairing and finite-dimensional dual-norm boundedness; the converse is exactly the accepted no-positive-exact-current criterion. Uniform class bounds give uniform linear mass bounds, while Poincare-dual test forms make the de Rham class continuous under weak current convergence, yielding weak compactness. The final subsequence argument proves closedness of the de Rham image cone, and positivity plus the mass estimate proves pointedness. The argument covers a zero-dimensional H^2 group and empty families, does not require h to be closed or Gauduchon, and makes no injectivity, uniqueness, nonlinear-mass, or varying-structure claim.
